Command: Do not offer burnt offerings in any place you choose
Summary: The command: Do not offer burnt offerings in any place you choose (Deuteronomy 12:13). Burnt offerings might be offered only in the place the LORD chose, not in every place that seemed right.
Commandment: Do not offer burnt offerings in any place you choose.
Application: It cannot be practised as written without the standing temple and Aaronic priesthood; its enduring lesson is God's holiness, the cost of atonement, and worship offered exactly as God appoints.
Purpose: Scripture's stated reason: offerings belonged in the place the LORD chose to put his name, lest worship fragment into every high place (Deuteronomy 12:13-14).
Function: Burnt offerings might be offered only in the place the LORD chose, not in every place that seemed right — a ceremonial law of one altar. Its goal was to keep worship from fragmenting into every high place, the offerings gathered where God put his name. The evil was private altars, each man offering where he pleased and worship scattering with him. It restrained that by the ban: not in any place you choose, but in the place the LORD chose, and the nation worshipped together.
